verdict.rationale: Secureframe's API reference has a documented 'Versioning' section. Additive changes stay backwards compatible, and breaking changes ship as a new dated API version, so the versioned-API half of the story is covered. The evidence does not describe any deprecation policy: no notice periods, sunset timelines, or support windows for older dated versions. Missing for 10: a documented deprecation/sunset policy with notice periods, a mechanism for pinning or selecting a specific dated version, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Backwards _incompatible_ changes require Secureframe to release a new dated API version, as the[y] can potentially break an integration.
Secureframe makes many additive API changes that are _backwards compatible_ and able to be supported in all API versions
